statement: He presented himself to the tribes at each pilgrimage season, camp by camp; Abu Lahab followed telling people not to listen.
notes: The report about Abu Lahab is in Musnad Ahmad from Rabi'ah ibn Abbad; reviewer to add the graded reference.

statement: Jabir: he presented himself to the people at the gathering place saying 'Is there any man who will take me to his people? Quraysh have prevented me from conveying the word of my Lord.'
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked; graded sahih (al-Albani, al-Arna'ut). The narration says 'at Arafat'.

statement: Yathrib lies about 250 miles north of Makkah; home of the Aws and Khazraj and of Jewish tribes.
The Aws and Khazraj had long been at war; Aishah: the day of Bu'ath was brought about by Allah for His Messenger; he came when they were divided and their leaders killed.
In the eleventh year he met six men of Khazraj at Aqabah; they recalled their Jewish neighbours' talk of a coming prophet, believed and returned.
notes: From Ibn Ishaq; the quoted words are reported speech of the six and are marked 'the historians report'.

statement: The following year twelve men came and pledged at Aqabah.

Ubadah ibn as-Samit: the terms of the pledge (no partners with Allah, no theft, no adultery, no killing of children, no invented slander, no disobedience in what is right); whoever fulfils it has his reward with Allah.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against both narrations; abridged (the part on expiation and concealment is omitted).

statement: Al-Bara: the first to come to us were Mus'ab ibn Umayr and Ibn Umm Maktum, who taught the people the Qur'an.
Mus'ab stayed with As'ad ibn Zurarah; Usayd ibn Hudayr and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh accepted Islam through him and their clan followed; Islam reached nearly every house.
In the thirteenth year seventy-three men and two women met him secretly at Aqabah in the last third of the night.

Jabir: the terms of the second pledge (hearing and obeying, spending, enjoining right and forbidding wrong, speaking for Allah without fear of blame, supporting and protecting him as their own families), with Paradise as the reward; they gave their hands.
notes: Musnad Ahmad, hadith of Jabir; graded sahih by al-Arna'ut and hasan by Ibn Kathir (from memory). Not in the datasets, so not machine-checked. Direct speech from memory. Held at grade C until the reviewer confirms; if confirmed, upgrade to B.

statement: Ka'b ibn Malik: I witnessed the night of Aqabah and would not exchange it for Badr, though Badr is more spoken of.
